name: Inbox · triage what needs me
model: Email-style three panes: folders, alert list, reading pane
why: Every office worker already knows this. The alerts are the 'emails'; open one and act with big buttons. Lowest learning curve.

name: Board · transports by stage
lang: Trello-like · DM Sans · purple · grey canvas
model: Kanban columns, drag cards between stages
why: Planning becomes moving cards. Status is position, not a label. Very easy to explain to new staff.

name: Grid · everything in one sheet
lang: Airtable-like · IBM Plex Sans · green · dense grid
model: Spreadsheet with filters, grouping, coloured pills, inline edit
why: Office workers live in Excel. Sortable, filterable, editable in place, exportable. Power without training.

name: Calendar · who drives when
model: Week calendar, drivers as coloured events; click empty slot to assign
why: Scheduling in the tool everybody already uses for meetings. Conflicts are overlaps; free time is white space.

name: Gantt · plan the week
lang: MS-Project-like · Source Sans 3 · orange · toolbar ribbon
model: Resource rows (trucks) × days, bars draggable, ribbon toolbar
why: Planners see utilisation and gaps across the week; drag a transport to another truck. Familiar to anyone who used Project.

name: Dark list · keyboard-first
model: Sidebar + list with keyboard shortcuts + command palette
why: For the fast dispatcher who lives on the keyboard: ⌘K to do anything, J/K to move, single-key actions shown in rows.

name: Live map · tap a truck
model: Full map, floating list panel, big rounded detail sheet
why: Feels like apps everyone uses on the phone. Answers 'where is it' instantly; detail slides in with one tap.

name: Assistant · ask in plain words
model: Chat with the operation; answers come as small tables and buttons
why: No menus to learn: 'who can take J-4218?' Answers carry the action buttons. Great for occasional users and managers.

name: Today · tiles + to-do
lang: Office dashboard · Work Sans · navy + yellow
model: Big number tiles, a to-do list, today's deliveries table
why: The manager's morning screen: how many, what's late, what to do. Readable from across the office.

name: Record · transport form
lang: Classic business app · Inter · slate · forms
model: Header with status + actions, tabs, two-column fields, activity log
why: Exactly how invoices and orders look in every ERP — editable fields, save, history. Zero surprise for back-office staff.

name: Checklist · today's run sheet
model: Time-ordered task list per transport with progress and big ticks
why: Dispatch as a checklist: things tick themselves when they happen; you only act on unchecked items with a red dot.

name: Board · high contrast
model: Giant type wallboard for the depot screen
why: For the screen on the office wall: readable from 6 m, no hover, no clutter. Problems in yellow, the rest in white on black.

name: Touch · yard tablet
lang: Touch-first · Nunito Sans · orange · huge targets
model: Two panes with 64px rows and thumb-sized buttons
why: For the yard or cais on a tablet: gloves-friendly buttons, one decision per screen, no tiny text.

name: Report · daily summary for the boss
lang: Editorial print · Source Serif 4 · black · A4 rhythm
model: One readable page: summary, exceptions, table, signatures
why: Some people want a page, not an app: emailed at 08:00 or printed for the morning meeting. Same data, zero interface.

name: Wizard · assign a driver in 3 steps
lang: Guided flow · Plus Jakarta Sans · cyan · stepper
model: Stepper with choice cards, recommendation badge, summary before confirm
why: For rare or risky tasks: the tool walks you through, ranks the options, and shows the consequences before you confirm.
